messages:
kelly: Hey @people-ops — planning to start parental leave on 2026-06-10. Quick Qs: what's the paperwork deadline, what do you need from me, and how should my team handle coverage?

mira (People Ops): Congrats, Kelly! :tada: For planned leaves we ask for at least 30 days notice when possible. Practical steps:
1) Submit a leave request in the HR portal: https://hr.redwood.example/leaves (New Request)
2) Choose leave type (primary/secondary caregiver) and enter start date
3) Upload supporting docs (birth/adoption or medical) within 15 calendar days of request
4) Fill out the "coverage plan" section so your manager can approve backups
If any dates are tight, DM me and we can fast-track.

kelly: Thanks — is there a specific file format for docs? and do I need to CC payroll?

mira (People Ops): PDF or image (jpg/png) is fine. No need to CC payroll manually; once you submit in the portal payroll gets notified automatically. You will get an email confirmation with a payroll case number.

tom: Team-side idea: 2-week overlap trial then rotate coverage. Proposal:
- Ana takes client A (handoff week: 1)
- Tom covers on-call for two weeks after handoff
- Weekly 30-min async check-ins with Kelly for 6 weeks (updates in #eng-oncall)

ana: I can take client A starting 2026-06-03 for the handoff week. :+1:

kelly: Appreciate it, Ana. Mira — how does pay/benefits work during leave? Will health insurance continue?

mira (People Ops): Short answer: benefits continue during approved parental leave. Details:
- Health/dental/vision: employer-sponsored coverage continues for the approved leave duration; employee deductions remain unless you opt out.
- Pay: Redwood provides different paid leave allotments by caregiver status — check your benefits summary in the portal for your exact weeks.
- PTO accrual: varies; I'll put your plan details in the portal summary.

people-ops-bot: automated reminder: "Upload supporting docs to HR portal to avoid payroll delays. Deadline: 2026-05-26 for full processing before start date."

tom: For coverage docs, add a short README in the repo with runbook links and critical contacts. That helps reduce questions mid-leave.

kelly: I'll add runbooks and schedule a 1-hour handoff on 2026-06-02. Anything else to track?

mira (People Ops): Please include expected return date in the portal. If you want a phased return (e.g., 60% hours for 4 weeks), note it in "notes" and we'll coordinate manager + People Ops. I'll schedule a checklist review 2 weeks before the start date to confirm payroll & coverage.

ana: I'll create a recurring calendar block for weekly check-ins so it's on everyone's calendar.

kelly: Thanks all! Submitting the portal request tonight and will ping you, Mira. :heart:
